note: Original places, batch 1 of 4: mines, quarries and workings. Each is a Location under a wild or city, linked to the ores found there. Written for Asetheria; no third-party text.

entries.name: The Green Gallery
entries.summary: A copper working in the Klynin foothills whose walls weep green, where miners cut malachite for paint and bead.
entries.body:
A long adit driven into the Klynin foothills along a vein of copper, and named for the colour of its walls: the rock is stained green to the roof, and in wet weather the water that runs down it is green too. The miners come for copper, but the real money is the banded green stone that lines the gallery, cut into beads and ground into paint.

## What is found here

The seams yield [[Malachite]] in plates and bosses, and the oxidised crust of the old timbers is scraped for [[Verdigris]]. Every tool in the gallery is wrapped in green dust by the end of a shift.

## Visiting

The Imperial surveyors keep a post at the mouth, because the spring-bearing range is jealously watched. A buyer with a stamp from Aeterna may enter; anyone else buys at the gate.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the gallery's drainage runs into a spring that feeds the capital's aqueduct, and copper in the water is the surveyors' real fear. A miner who knows the truth would sell it.

entries.name: Blue-Vein Pit
entries.summary: An open pit in the desert where blue copper ore and sky-blue stone are dug out of red rock by the thousand baskets.
entries.body:
An open pit sunk into the red rock of the great desert, where a vein of blue copper ore runs close to the surface. The work is done by gangs with baskets and ropes, and the dust of the pit is the same blue as the stone, so a gang coming up at dusk looks like a procession of ghosts.

## What is found here

The pit gives [[Azurite]] for pigment and, in the deeper cuts, small pockets of [[Lapis]] that the foremen pocket before the weigh-house sees them.

## Visiting

Caravans stop at the pit's cistern, and a trader can buy ground blue by the pound at a price that rises with every day's distance from the pit.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the foremen's skimming of lapis is an open secret. A visitor who reports it gets a reward from the satrap and a knife from the foremen.

entries.name: The Yellow Cleft
entries.summary: A sulphur-stained crack in the high rock where gold-yellow and blood-red poison-stones are mined by men who do not expect to be old.
entries.body:
A narrow crack in the Olympus rock, yellow at the lip and red at the bottom, where the mineral that painters call gold and poisoners call something else is dug out by hand. The smell is garlic and struck matches, and the men who work here cover their faces with wet cloth and are paid twice the going rate.

## What is found here

The upper wall gives [[Orpiment]]; the deeper cuts give [[Realgar]]. Both are bright, both are brittle, and both are poison. Painters pay for them, and so do the other kind of buyer.

## Visiting

The cleft is a day's climb above the last shepherd's hut. A guide is a good idea and a mask is a better one.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a rival buyer has been paying the miners to mark the rock with a cross when a seam is rich, and a rich seam has been collapsing within a week.

entries.name: The Lodestone Shelf
entries.summary: A bare ledge on the Oros range where iron ore pulls a compass needle off true and shepherds will not sleep.
entries.body:
A broad grey ledge high on the Oros range, bare of grass, where the iron ore is so strong that a sailor's needle swings off north and a loose nail will creep across a table. The shepherds will not pasture their flocks here, because the sheep will not settle, and they tell of a man who tied his boots with iron and could not leave.

## What is found here

The ledge is the best source of [[Lodestone]] on the coast. A good piece lifts a handful of nails and fetches a month's wages in any port town with a chart-maker.

## Visiting

The shelf is open to anyone willing to climb to it. The only ones who do are the stone-hunters, who go in pairs and leave their metal behind.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a compass is useless across the whole shelf, and a party that loses its way there will find their steel tools useless too.

entries.name: The Jet Strand
entries.summary: A black cliff-foot on the Tiberius where polished jet and honey-coloured amber wash up after the spring floods.
entries.body:
A stretch of black clay cliff below the Tiberius' upper reaches, where the spring floods cut the bank and leave the shore strewn with dark, light stones. Local children collect them and sell to the dealers who come up from the capital with bags and short tempers.

## What is found here

The cliff gives [[Jet]], black and warm in the hand, and the flood-wrack sometimes carries a lump of [[Northern Amber]] that has travelled down the river from somewhere far to the north.

## Visiting

The strand is public, and in the first week after a flood it is crowded with collectors. After that, the dealers have bought it all.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a piece of amber with something trapped in it, a seal or a ring, has been found twice. Someone is dropping them upstream.

entries.name: The Natron Pans
entries.summary: White crusted flats on the shore of Varathros Lake where the lake gives up its salt, soda and a smell like old eggs.
entries.body:
A series of shallow basins along the shore of Varathros Lake that fill in the wet season and bake to a white crust in the dry. The crust is natron: a soda-salt used for glass, for cleaning, for embalming and for the washing of the dead. The workers rake it into heaps and wear cloths over their eyes against the glare.

## What is found here

The pans are the main source of [[Natron]] for every glass-house on the coast and every embalmer in the south.

## Visiting

A cart-road runs from the pans to the lake's southern port, and the hauliers are a hard, silent breed who work by moonlight to avoid the heat.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the crust has a layer of something older beneath it. A worker who raked too deep hauled up a bronze mask and stopped talking.

entries.name: Smoke-Steps
entries.summary: A stair of yellow terraces climbing the warm flank of Vael'Tharan, where the mountain breathes sulphur and the fire-stone glows at night.
entries.body:
A natural stair of yellow terraces on the warm flank of Vael'Tharan, cut by generations of sulphur-gatherers. Vents along the steps breathe a pale smoke that smells of struck flints, and at night some of the stones glow a dull red, as if the mountain were remembering the fire that broke the Titans.

## What is found here

The steps are crusted with [[Brimstone]], scraped off in sheets, and the hottest vents leave glassy lumps of [[Fire-Stone]] that stay warm for days after they are cut.

## Visiting

The gatherers work in the cool of dawn and are off the mountain by noon. A traveller who stays later has been warned.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the glowing stones are brighter each year, and the gatherers' chief has begun to leave offerings. He will not say to whom.

entries.name: The Pentelic Terraces
entries.summary: White-and-gold quarry steps on the Oros range, the source of the marble that every Hellenorian temple wants and few can afford.
entries.body:
A flight of enormous quarry terraces cut into the Oros range, each step a clean wall of fine white stone with a faint golden cast where the iron weathers out of it. The cut blocks are lowered on timber ramps to the road, and the road is worn into a trench by eight centuries of ox-carts.

## What is found here

The terraces produce [[Pentelic Marble]], the stone of the finest temples on the coast. A block from the upper steps has been quoted at the price of a ship.

## Visiting

The quarry-masters admit visitors on feast days and let them walk the lower steps. The upper ones are for the cutters and the stone-priests.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the upper terraces have been closed for a year, officially for safety. A cutter says they cut into a hollow and found a carved floor.

entries.name: The Lamplit Quarries
entries.summary: Marble quarries cut underground by lamplight on an island in the sea-fog, where the stone glows faintly when it is cut.
entries.body:
A set of galleries mined from beneath, by lamplight, in an island's marble heart on the edge of the sea-fog. The stone is translucent enough that a lamp held behind a thin slab shows through, and the cutters work by lamp because the galleries are too deep and the fog too thick for daylight.

## What is found here

The galleries yield [[Lamp-Quarried Marble]], prized for statues because it takes light into the flesh. A cutter's wage is good, and his lungs are not.

## Visiting

Boats come in on the tide, guided by a bell. The quarry-master will let a sculptor in and no one else.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the fog around the island has a voice, and the night shift reports that it knows their names.

entries.name: The Purple Quarry
entries.summary: A royal quarry in the desert hills, closed to all but the emperor's cutters, where the stone of kings is dug out of the red hills.
entries.body:
A guarded quarry in the red hills of the desert, worked by convicts and imperial cutters and closed to everyone else by a wall and a garrison. The stone is purple-red, speckled white, and a column of it is a boast of the highest order. The road out is paved just for the stone, and the carts that use it are marked with the royal seal.

## What is found here

The quarry gives [[Imperial Porphyry]], reserved for the highest office, and the grey-pink granite called [[Red Syenite]] from the lower faces, which any builder may buy.

## Visiting

A visitor needs a seal from the satrap. Without one, the garrison does not ask questions.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the convicts have been carving something into the hidden walls of the pit. A guard who looked has requested a transfer.

entries.name: The Alabaster Cuttings
entries.summary: Honey-white cuttings on the flank of Kharveth, where soft stone is carved into lamps and perfume jars and the wind carries white dust.
entries.body:
A set of pale cuttings low on the mountain of Kharveth, where the stone is so soft that a mason can carve it with a knife. It is white with a warm honey cast, and a lamp placed inside a jar of it glows like a coal. The workshops at the foot of the cuttings turn out perfume jars, lamp-bowls and burial urns by the thousand.

## What is found here

The cuttings yield [[Alabaster]], easy to carve and slow to forgive a careless blow. A finished jar is worth ten times the block.

## Visiting

The carvers sell from the workshop doors, and the market at the cuttings' foot is the place to buy a gift of the stone.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the qanat-diggers refuse to sink a shaft on this mountain and the carvers cannot say why they never carve the lowest cutting.

entries.name: The Salt Cathedral
entries.summary: A vast hall carved by miners out of a salt dome beneath the black ridge, with pillars of crystal and a chapel the miners keep.
entries.body:
A cavernous working beneath the Zaruk'thal Spine, hollowed out of a dome of rock salt by centuries of miners and left standing on pillars of salt they chose not to cut. The hall rings when a man speaks and glitters when a lamp is lit, and the miners have carved a chapel at one end and a saint's niche at the other.

## What is found here

The walls give [[Deep Rock Salt]] in clear and grey blocks, hauled up on rope and sold from the pit-head by weight.

## Visiting

The miners lead a tour for a small fee and a larger tip. The chapel has a lamp that has not gone out in living memory.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the miners say a second hall lies beneath this one, and that the lamp in the chapel is there to keep something from walking up.

entries.name: Lime-Burners' Hollow
entries.summary: A smoky hollow in the plains where kilns burn day and night, and builders come for lime and the grey volcanic sand that sets under water.
entries.body:
A hollow in the Latium plains ringed by squat stone kilns, burning limestone to quicklime day and night. The smoke hangs in the hollow like fog, the burners are grey from hair to boot, and the sound of the place is the clatter of carts and the rasp of coughing.

## What is found here

The kilns turn out [[Quicklime]], and a pit on the hollow's north rim yields [[Pozzolana]], the grey volcanic sand that makes mortar set hard even under water.

## Visiting

Builders from every city of the Imperium send an agent to the hollow, and the agents lodge in a long, dusty inn called The Whitewash.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the burners have a custom of leaving the oldest kiln unlit. They say it was last fired for a body.

entries.name: The Kohl Workings
entries.summary: Grey-black pits in the dry gorge where a soft, shining stone is dug for eye-paint and for the women who sell it.
entries.body:
A scatter of shallow pits along the Parthian Ravine, where a soft grey-black stone is dug by women and boys and carried to the grinding-sheds at the gorge's mouth. Ground fine and mixed with fat, it becomes the dark eye-paint worn from the palace to the caravan road.

## What is found here

The pits yield [[Kohl-Stone]]. It is cheap at the pit and dear at the court, and the difference is what feeds the gorge.

## Visiting

The sheds sell to any trader who comes with a mule and a good manner. The women who run them do not haggle twice.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: one grinder mixes a pinch of something else into the paint she sells to the garrison officers. The effect is slow.

entries.name: Bloodstone Scree
entries.summary: A long slope of dark green stone flecked with red, where, they say, the blood of a hero turned the rock.
entries.body:
A long slope of loose dark-green stone on the Oros range, flecked with red as if splashed. The shepherds tell that a hero was wounded here and that his blood turned the rock, and the stone-hunters, who do not believe it, come anyway.

## What is found here

The scree holds [[Bloodstone]], red-flecked and heavy, carried by soldiers as a charm against wounds, and pebbles of banded [[Seal Jasper]] that the engravers buy by the sack.

## Visiting

The slope is steep and loose. A climber who disturbs it brings down a slide of stones that rattle like a bag of coins.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: one stone near the top is flecked with fresh red. It stays wet when the weather is dry.

entries.name: Emery Shore
entries.summary: A black, glinting beach where the sea grinds a hard grey stone to powder that polishers pay well for.
entries.body:
A short black beach on the Aeolus strait where a hard grey rock breaks from the headland and is ground to grit by the surf. The beach glints in the sun, and the grit is gathered by hand into sacks and carried up a goat-path to the polishers' sheds.

## What is found here

The beach is the source of [[Island Emery]], the abrasive that cuts gems, marble and, if one is patient, steel.

## Visiting

The gatherers live in huts above the beach and sell to the sea-captains who call. The wind here is the strait's own, and it carries a sting.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a gatherer's child has found a ring in the grit with the mark of a shipwrecked house. The family wants it sold quietly.

entries.name: The Pumice Flats
entries.summary: A grey shore where the sea throws up floating stone, and every boy on the strait knows how to sell it.
entries.body:
A wide flat shore on the strait where, after a storm, the sea deposits a drift of grey, floating rock: light as bread, rough as a cat's tongue. Boys comb the tideline at dawn with baskets, and the drift is sold by the sack to scribes, bathers and anyone with a callus.

## What is found here

The shore gives [[Pumice]], and in the dunes behind it the gatherers turn up chips of [[Black Flint]] washed out of the chalk.

## Visiting

The flats are open to all. After a storm there is a market at the north end that sells the drift by the sack and the boys by the day.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: after the last great storm the drift included a floating island of pumice with a door in it.

entries.name: The Carnelian Washings
entries.summary: Dry riverbeds in the desert where red and green stones are sifted from gravel by lines of washers in the cold of dawn.
entries.body:
A set of dry riverbeds in the desert's northern fringe where, in the season of flash floods, red and green pebbles are washed from the hills and left in the gravel. The washers work in lines in the cold of dawn, sifting with wicker trays and calling out each good stone like a bid.

## What is found here

The gravel gives [[Carnelian]], warm as a sunset, and now and again a fleck of green [[Desert Emerald]] that sets the whole line cheering.

## Visiting

A washer's licence is cheap. The stones are not, and the dealers' tents at the end of the line are guarded.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the dealers fix the price at dusk; a washer who breaks the ring is found in the dry bed by the following dawn.

entries.name: The Gods' Table Grotto
entries.summary: A shining cave high on Olympus whose walls are lined with clear crystal, and where, shepherds say, the gods once dined.
entries.body:
A cave high on the Olympus range, its walls lined with clear, six-sided crystal that throws a morning sunbeam into a hundred points. A flat slab at the cave's centre has been called the gods' table since before the first shepherd, and offerings of oil and wine are left on it.

## What is found here

The walls yield [[Mountain Crystal]], clear as ice and cold in the hand, cut for lenses, cups and the eyes of statues.

## Visiting

A priest of the mountain keeps the way and charges for the climb. He says the gods dislike company, and the offering plate says otherwise.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the table has been wiped clean every morning for a week, and the priest says he has not done it.

entries.name: The Calamine Diggings
entries.summary: Pale pits in the Klynin hills where brass-makers buy the stone that turns copper to gold, and a bitter salt crusts the walls.
entries.body:
A set of pale, crumbling pits in the lower Klynin hills, where the ore that brass-makers call the gold-maker is dug and the workings are crusted with a bitter white salt. The diggers wear scarves and complain of a taste in the mouth that never leaves.

## What is found here

The pits give [[Calamine]], which turns smelted copper to brass, and the crusts on the pit walls are scraped for [[Alum]], used by dyers to fix colour.

## Visiting

Brass-founders from Mavelon keep a standing contract here and send a wagon each week. A free buyer pays a premium.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the diggers have begun to find old tools in the lowest cut, made of a metal no one has seen. They are quietly selling them.

entries.name: The Red-Earth Sheds
entries.summary: Long sheds behind the sanctuary where red clay is washed, dried and sealed in jars for painters and the pious.
entries.body:
A row of long sheds behind the sanctuary of the temple-port, where the red earth dug from a hill across the bay is washed in troughs, dried in trays and sealed in small jars with the sanctuary's stamp. The workers have red hands and red hair, and so do their children.

## What is found here

The sheds prepare [[Sinopic Red]], the colour of a painter's best vermilion earth, sold to artists and, in a smaller jar, to pilgrims who rub it on their foreheads.

## Visiting

The sheds are open to pilgrims after the morning rite. The priests encourage questions, and the shopkeeper encourages purchases.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the jar's stamp is forged in the port's lower market. The sanctuary has not noticed, or has decided not to.

entries.name: The Glass-Stone Cellars
entries.summary: Cool cellars under the river city where sheets of clear mineral are split for windows by men who work in silence.
entries.body:
A warren of cool cellars beneath the river city where blocks of clear, layered mineral are split into thin sheets with a wooden wedge. The cellars are silent by custom, because a shout can crack a sheet from end to end, and the splitters speak in a sign language of their own.

## What is found here

The cellars produce [[Window-Stone]], the pane that lets light through a house before glass is cheap. A sheet the size of a door is a rich man's boast.

## Visiting

A buyer is admitted to the front cellar and told to whisper. The back cellars are closed.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the guild's silence rule has hidden a murder. A splitter's body lay in the third cellar for two days before anyone said so.

entries.name: The Chalk Downs
entries.summary: Rolling white hills where black flint lies in the chalk like plums in a pudding, and the flint-knappers have worked since before the empires.
entries.body:
Smooth white hills on the Latium plains, so thin in soil that the chalk shows through the turf like bone. Dark nodules of flint lie in the chalk in bands, and the flint-knappers who work them are the oldest trade on the plains: their fathers made spear-points here when the empires were villages.

## What is found here

The downs give [[Black Flint]], struck into blades, sparks and building-stone, and the old pits are still open for any who ask.

## Visiting

A knapper's yard on the downs will sell a fire-kit or a flint blade for a copper. The best tool-makers are the old women who say little and charge less.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a barrow on the highest down was opened last year. What was found has been quietly reburied by order of a district magistrate.

entries.name: The Cinnabar Shafts
entries.summary: Deep, hot shafts in the mountain's side where red ore is cut by condemned men, and the air is poison to anyone who stays.
entries.body:
A set of narrow shafts sunk into the mountain's red side, worked by prisoners under guard because no free man will take the job. The ore is bright red, the air is thick and sweet-tasting, and a man who works the face for a year loses his teeth, then his hands' steadiness, then his mind.

## What is found here

The shafts give [[Cinnabar]], the red ore of quicksilver and the best vermilion, and the cap-rock above them holds flecks of brassy [[Devil's Gold]] that fools take home.

## Visiting

The shafts are fenced and the road is watched. A buyer deals with the overseer at the lower gate and never goes up.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a prisoner has smuggled out a plate of silver-white metal that flows like water and will not be held. He will trade it for his life.

entries.name: The Pitch Seep
entries.summary: A black pool in the dry gorge where tar rises through the rock and a thin, burning oil floats on the water.
entries.body:
A broad pool in the Parthian Ravine where black tar seeps from a crack in the rock and spreads across a pond of stagnant water, with a clear, sharp-smelling oil floating on top. Bones lie round the edge of the pool, and the gatherers do not wade in without a rope.

## What is found here

The seep gives [[Black Pitch]], dug in lumps and used to seal hulls and roofs, and the floating oil is skimmed as [[Persian Naphtha]], the fluid that burns on water and that armies pay a king's ransom to hold.

## Visiting

A garrison post guards the pool. The soldiers keep it a state secret that anyone who can smell is in on.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the oil has begun to burn by itself in the heat of the day. The garrison commander is hiding the fires from the satrap.

entries.name: The Turquoise Diggings
entries.summary: A sky-coloured scar on a dry hill where the satrap's miners follow robin's-egg veins, and every stone is counted.
entries.body:
A scar of blue-green rock on a dry hill, worked in a honeycomb of galleries too low to stand in. The miners are paid by the stone and searched at the gate, and the satrap's clerks count every piece by colour before a sack is sealed. A hard stone is worth more than a ruby here, and a soft one is worth a flogging if it goes missing.

## What is found here

The diggings give [[Nishapur Turquoise]] in veins and nodules, and the best stones go to the king's own jewellers.

## Visiting

A licensed dealer may buy at the weigh-house on market days. Everyone else sees the hill from the road.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a missing stone, said to be the size of a pigeon's egg, is the reason for the new searches. The miners know where it is.

entries.name: The Travertine Cuts
entries.summary: Warm white terraces beside the river where hot springs lay down stone as fast as the quarrymen cut it.
entries.body:
A line of pale terraces beside the Tiberius where hot springs run over the rock and lay down a creamy stone as fast as the quarrymen cut it. The cuts look like frozen waterfalls, and the pools between them are warm enough for bathing in winter.

## What is found here

The cuts give [[Tiburtine Stone]], the pale, pitted building stone of half the capital, and the older heaps of volcanic [[Tufa Stone]] that the builders keep for backing walls.

## Visiting

A bathhouse by the springs charges for the pools. The quarrymen are happy to be sketched by passing painters, who pay in drawings.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the spring's flow has changed twice this year. A hydrologist from the capital believes someone is diverting it.
